2.33(b)(3)
Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
During a review of facility records, the following non-compliance involving a lack of timely communication of health
findings to the attending veterinarian was observed. On February 17, 2026, a calf was received for a heart study. The
following 2 days, animal care staff reported blood in the feces to the veterinary resident twice but no physical exam or
testing was performed and the attending veterinarian was not notified. Care staff observed additional symptoms including
restlessness, vocalization, and loss of appetite on the 3rd and 4th day after arrival which was again not reported to the
attending veterinarian. On the 5th day after arrival (February 23) the calf was observed to have lost approximately 8lb. It
was not until this point when diagnostics were performed that the attending veterinarian was notified of the health
problems in this animal. Treatment was provided and the calf's symptoms improved but the animal was euthanized due to
being a poor candidate for the study.
Failure to communicate health problems to the attending veterinarian in a timely manner may result in unnecessary
discomfort in the animals.
The facility must establish and maintain a program of veterinary care that includes daily observations with a mechanism of
direct and frequent communication so that timely and accurate information on problems of animal health are conveyed to
the attending veterinarian.
Correct by: Corrected at the time of inspection. Continue to ensure animal health problems are communicated to the
attending veterinarian in a timely manner from 7/14/26 forward.
2.38(f)(1)
Miscellaneous.
During a review of facility records, the following non-compliance involving animal handling was observed. On February 14,
2026, a rabbit was found in a housing room outside its cage. It was discovered the 3rd level cage door was unlatched and
open. The rabbit was diagnosed with a fractured nail on the right forelimb. The rabbit was treated with anti-inflammatory
medications and recovered without incident.
Failure to handle animals in a careful manner, including failing to secure cage latches to keep animals contained to their
enclosures, may result in injury to the animals.
Handling of all animals must be done as carefully as possible in a manner that does not cause trauma or physical harm.
Correct by: Corrected at the time of inspection. Continue to ensure animals are handled in a careful manner from 7/14/26
forward.

3.127(b)
Facilities, outdoor.
During a review of facility records, the following non-compliance involving lack of shelter from inclement weather was
observed. On November 25, 2025, three sheep were inadvertently locked out of the barn with only access to the paddock
and pasture for approximately 22 hours. During this period, the animals did not have access to shelter. The animals also
did not have access to water but there were no signs of dehydration observed. The door between the outdoor area and
the barn is normally kept open but was found closed, blocking the animals' access inside.
Failure to provide shelter can result in discomfort to the animals.
Natural or artificial shelter shall be provided for all animals kept outdoors to afford them protection and to prevent
discomfort to such animals.
Correct by: Corrected at the time of inspection. Continue to ensure all animals housed outdoors have access to shelter
from 7/14/26 forward.



This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the attending veterinarian.

2.31(c)(7)               Critical
Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
82 naked mole rats were euthanized by a method not on the approved protocol between 9/26/2025 and 10/3/2025. The
naked mole rats were euthanized by CO2 instead of the injectable euthanasia method approved in the protocol. Naked
mole rats are a hypoxia tolerant species, and the use of CO2 required a prolonged exposure of ~40 minutes to achieve
death.
Failure to follow the approved protocol and making unapproved changes does not allow the IACUC to review these
changes as required and ensure the animals involved do not experience negative impacts to their health and welfare.
The IACUC must ensure that all significant changes regarding the care and use of animals in ongoing activities including
euthanasia are reviewed and approved prior to implementation.

Corrective action was implemented prior to this inspection.
To be corrected from this day forward, July 7, 2026
2.33(b)(4)               Critical
Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
A rabbit died during an anesthetic procedure on 12/11/2025. The animal’s depth of anesthesia had become too light and
the anesthetic gas level was increased. The level was not reduced once a deeper plane of anesthesia was achieved and
the animal subsequently died during the procedure and was not able to be resuscitated.
Failure to appropriately monitor patients and adjust anesthetic levels during a procedure can lead to injury or death of the
patient.
Each research facility must establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that provide adequate guidance
to personnel involved in the care and use of animals regarding handling, immobilization, anesthesia. analgesia,
tranquilization, and euthanasia.
Corrective action was implemented prior to this inspection.
To be corrected from this day forward, July 7, 2026



This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative.

2.31(c)(7)
Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
A review of records for pig #38309 indicate that on June 1, 2026 the animal underwent a surgical procedure as described
in the associated IACUC approved protocol #202300000039. Records show that the administration of anesthetic and
analgesic agents deviated from what was described in the protocol, resulting in the animal receiving multiple doses of
Ketamine and an additional dose of Xylazine. In addition, the pig did not receive an oral dose of Meloxicam pre-
operatively nor an intra-operative Bupivacaine intercostal injection.
Failure to follow the approved protocol and making unapproved changes does not allow the IACUC to review these
changes as required and ensure the animals involved do not experience negative impacts to their health and welfare. The
IACUC must ensure that all significant changes regarding the care and use of animals in ongoing activities are reviewed
and approved prior to implementation. Currently, the IACUC has initiated preliminary steps towards correction.
******Correct by August 31, 2026
2.31(d)(1)(ii)
Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
IACUC approved Protocol #202300000039 did not provide a written narrative description of the methods and sources
used to determine that alternatives were not available to procedures that are included in the protocol that may cause more
than momentary pain or distress to the animals (thoracotomy and tracheotomy).
The IACUC shall determine that the principal investigator has considered alternatives to procedures that may cause more
than momentary or slight pain or distress to the animals and has provided a written narrative description of the methods
and sources used to determine that alternatives were not available. These requirements ensure that all procedures
contained in the protocol minimize discomfort, distress, and pain to the animals. The IACUC needs to address this item
identified for this protocol.
***********Correct by August 31, 2026



This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
